blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Arbitrum carries approximately 97.26% of the four positive pinned token supplies; Ethereum, Base and Plume are individually below ten percent. Every current token proxy is upgradeable and has a nonzero transferRestrictor and accessControl, both naming the shared dispatcher. A live EOA has role-zero administration and role-four upgrade authority on all four deployments; canCall for restrict(address) is also true. Current deployed token and restrictor source parity, holder-targeting enforcement and the complete active restrictor-role inventory remain unverified, so this review records the directly evidenced implementation-replacement exposure as Possible rather than upgrading old-version blacklist source into an active Yes verdict. No renunciation or absence of holder restrictions is asserted.

oracleRisk.summary: USD+ distributes Treasury-linked returns through its token supply index. Current token version-five index/rate setters and their exact pricing authority are not source-verified; an observed index and a fixed-dollar redemption target do not prove external or independent valuation.

branchApplicability.rationale: The issuer describes a Treasury-backed holder token with wallet-balance yield and direct issuer redemption. No USD+ borrower collateral or liquidation branches are identified. Pinned balancePerShare and publicVersion observations establish current index accounting, but the publicly available version-one rebasing source does not establish the deployed version-five rate-setter or external-price dependencies.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Four reviewed deployments support issuer-native minting through the documented Minter. The issuer app also offers bridging, but the exact transfer rail, liability netting and bridge-specific mint, upgrade, peer and validation controllers have not been verified. Native issuance observations do not certify absence of bridge exposure.
